problem:
Calculate $∇\cdot (2F+G)$ for the vector fields $F$ and $G,$ where

$$
F={e}^{5x}\,i+y{e}^{3y}\,j,\,∇\cdot G=3{e}^{5x}-2{e}^{3y}.
$$
worked_solution:
If $F$ and $G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following  linearity properties for divergence:

- $∇\cdot (kF)=k∇\cdot F$

- $∇\cdot (F+G)=∇\cdot F+∇\cdot G.$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot (2F+G) & =∇\cdot (2F)+∇\cdot G \\  & =2∇\cdot F+∇\cdot G.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to calculate $∇\cdot F.$ In doing so, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({e}^{5x})+\frac{∂}{∂y}(y{e}^{3y}) \\  & =5{e}^{5x}+{e}^{3y}+3y{e}^{3y}.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the linearity properties, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot (2F+G) & =2∇\cdot F+∇\cdot G \\  & =2\cdot (5{e}^{5x}+{e}^{3y}+3y{e}^{3y})+3{e}^{5x}-2{e}^{3y} \\  & =10{e}^{5x}+2{e}^{3y}+6y{e}^{3y}+3{e}^{5x}-2{e}^{3y} \\  & =13{e}^{5x}+6y{e}^{3y}.\end{aligned}
$$
